entries.value: Build roads, complete city contracts, and collect tolls
A new city is generated every game, including rivers, stations, airports and ports.

Character: select the character button to view heroes, abilities and statistics. “Choose one of two” lets you pick between two random heroes and starting contracts; “Random” assigns one immediately.

“Logistics Magnate”: companies transport perishable, heavy and hazardous cargo from hubs. One construction round and {0} transport rounds. Moves are planned in secret; trucks move together, and overloaded roads become congested.

You run a road company. Build links between locations, complete city contracts to connect districts and earn tolls from opponents using your roads. The highest-scoring player wins.
Optional; does not use the main action
…then the next player takes their turn. A new round begins after everyone has acted.

Your main action is one of three: draw two resource cards (one can be a luck card), build a road by paying its resource cost, or draw contracts and keep at least one. Instead of building, you can upgrade a road to a highway.
Road building scores points; longer roads are more valuable.
Road color identifies the required resource. A road of length 3 costs three matching cards. White roads accept any one resource type. Click a card to flip it.
City streets are the most common road type.
Avenues and ring roads are long and profitable.
Machinery replaces any card. Taking face-up machinery as the first draw ends card drawing for that turn.
A contract connects two districts using any of their locations. Completed contracts earn points; unfinished ones lose points at the end.
Tolls are charged as soon as you complete a contract, using the cheapest available route. Later upgrades do not raise that fee, and building your own detour later will not refund it.
Try It: Connect a Contract Route
Complex contracts earn more points, but carry larger penalties:
Transit contract: a single route from A to B via C.
Hub contract: district A is connected to B and C.
New locations, roads and contracts open on the outskirts.

Highways have an orange outline; roads built during rush hour look similar.
